title: Shell on Seven Mile
subject: a Detroit man whose forty-year-old pet tortoise Big Ron escapes the backyard and is found three blocks away at the car wash on Seven Mile, where the whole crew starts chanting his name
caption: Detroit ghettotech, fast Detroit club style with electro and booty bass roots. Pounding Roland 808 kick and rapid snare rolls; a deep booty-bass sub; short electro synth stabs; heavy handclaps on every beat. Raw fast club mix, crowded and loud, chants up front. Male MC with chanted call-and-response hooks, a party crowd shouting back. 150 BPM, G minor. Rowdy, silly and party-loud. No trap hi-hats, no autotune, no melodic pop chorus, no house piano, no dubstep wobble.
lyrics:
[Intro - 808 kick and claps, MC count-in]

[Verse 1]
Gate swung open in the night
Big Ron gone, there's no shell in sight
Forty years old and he's moving slow
Where did he go, where did he go

[Chorus]
Big Ron, Big Ron, shell on Seven Mile
Big Ron, Big Ron, walking with a style
Slow, slow, slow, slow
Big Ron, Big Ron, where'd you go

[Verse 2]
Lady from the car wash on the phone
Says a tortoise blocking bay number one
Suds on his back and he will not move
Whole line honking, Ron's in the groove

[Chorus]
Big Ron, Big Ron, shell on Seven Mile
Big Ron, Big Ron, foam in his smile
Slow, slow, slow, slow
Big Ron, Big Ron, take it slow

[Bridge - kick and claps only]
Put him in the wagon, put him in the back
Crew on the sidewalk chanting him back

[Outro - crowd chant, kick fades]
Ron, Ron, Ron, Ron
Shined up shell and he's coming home
